claims.text: Overall Orange Flood in China (event id 1104081, episode 7, reporting window 31 Jul 2026 01:00 UTC to 13 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC). Heavy rain associated with Typhoon Dolphin caused flooding in Hubei Province, China, from 11 August 2026.

GDACS's current flood report for event FL-2026-000148-CHN (reporting window 31 July - 1 September 2026) states 'Death: 1' and 'Displaced: 309701', down from 326,643 displaced and 2 deaths in the prior read; overall alert level remains Orange (medium humanitarian impact).

GDACS event API data for FL 1104081: displaced total 237338, with 215,600 people evacuated in Shanghai, China (8-10 August 2026) as the single largest component, and further evacuations totaling over 238,000 across Shaanxi, Hubei, Zhejiang and Jiangsu combined. Event location centroid: latitude 32.2656, longitude 111.6474. Date range 2026-07-31T01:00:00 to 2026-08-13T01:00:00.

GDACS's flood report (event FL-2026-000148-CHN, id 1104081) as of 16 August 2026 rates the event an Orange alert (medium humanitarian impact) centered on Henan Province flooding driven by the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin, with 302,931 people displaced and 0 deaths recorded; China's Ministry of Emergency Management dispatched 13 emergency drainage teams to Zhoukou city for urban waterlogging relief.

GDACS's flood report for event FL-2026-000148-CHN (episode 9, reporting window now 31 July - 16 August 2026) records the event's first confirmed death and missing persons: 1 person killed and 3 people missing after a residential building collapsed in a debris flow in Heping Town, Changxing County, Huzhou, Zhejiang Province. The combined displacement total remains 302,931 people evacuated across Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Shanghai, Zhejiang and Jiangsu; overall alert level remains Orange (medium humanitarian impact).

GDACS's flood report for event FL-2026-000148-CHN (episode 10, reporting window 31 July - 19 August 2026) records 309,701 people displaced, up from 302,931 in episode 9, with newly reported evacuations in Sichuan Province added to the affected areas; the death toll remains 1 with 3 missing in Zhejiang, and GDACS's event-data API additionally records 134 people rescued and 151 buildings damaged or destroyed. Overall alert level remains Orange (medium humanitarian impact).

GDACS's flood report for event FL-2026-000148-CHN (episode 11, reporting window 31 July - 25 August 2026) records 314,734 people displaced, up from 309,701 in episode 10, with newly reported evacuations in Guangxi Province added to the affected areas; the death toll remains 1 with 3 missing in Zhejiang, 134 rescued and 151 buildings damaged or destroyed (unchanged). Overall alert level remains Orange.

GDACS's flood report for event FL-2026-000148-CHN (episode 13, as of 24 August 2026; event dates 31 July - 25 August 2026) records 2 deaths and 319,550 people displaced, and remains an Orange alert: 'Flood can have a medium humanitarian impact based on the magnitude, exposed population and vulnerability.'

GDACS's current flood report for event FL-2026-000148-CHN (episode 10 per the report page, reporting window 31 July - 26 August 2026) records 326,643 people displaced (up from 319,550 in the prior read) and 2 deaths (unchanged), remaining an overall Orange alert.

description: Flooding tied to Typhoon Dolphin has affected eight provinces and municipalities across central and eastern China since 31 July 2026. GDACS's current flood report (reporting window 31 July - 1 September 2026) records 309,701 people displaced and 1 confirmed death, down from a peak of 326,643 displaced and 2 deaths in its prior read; GDACS's own confirmed-death count has fluctuated between 1 and 2 across recent episode updates. The first death and 3 missing came when a residential building collapsed in a debris flow in Changxing County, Zhejiang, and GDACS's event-data API has recorded 134 people rescued and 151 buildings damaged or destroyed. The event remains at Orange alert.

updates.text: GDACS's flood report window extended to 1 September, with displaced population down to 309,701 (from 326,643) and the recorded death toll at 1 (from 2 in the prior read); the event remains at Orange alert.
GDACS's flood report window extended to 26 August, with displaced population up to 326,643 (from 319,550) and the death toll unchanged at 2; the event remains at Orange alert.

GDACS's episode 13 update (24 August) raised the displacement total to 319,550 (from 314,734 in episode 11) and the recorded death toll to 2 (from 1); the event remains at Orange alert with its reporting window extended to 25 August.

GDACS's episode 11 update raised the combined displacement total to 314,734 (from 309,701) and added evacuations in Guangxi Province; the death toll remained 1 with 3 missing, 134 rescued and 151 buildings damaged or destroyed.

GDACS's episode 10 update raised the combined displacement total to 309,701 (from 302,931) and added evacuations in Sichuan Province to the affected areas; the death toll remained 1 with 3 missing, and GDACS's event-data API additionally recorded 134 people rescued and 151 buildings damaged or destroyed.

GDACS's episode 9 update recorded the event's first confirmed casualties: 1 person killed and 3 missing after a residential building collapsed in a debris flow in Heping Town, Changxing County, Huzhou, Zhejiang Province; the combined displacement total held at 302,931 people.

China's Ministry of Emergency Management dispatched 13 emergency drainage teams to Zhoukou city, Henan, for urban waterlogging relief, with GDACS keeping the event at Orange alert, 302,931 people displaced and no deaths then recorded.
GDACS raised the combined evacuation total to 302,931 people, up from 237,338, across Hubei, Henan, Shaanxi, Shanghai, Zhejiang and Jiangsu.
